title: Close remaining assessment identity gaps
status_note: Round 2 after verifier back_to_worker: F1 and F2 fixed; the optional blank-part rule and the #NA/1.#QNAN spellings were added. Empty parts were deliberately left accepted. The reviewed-profile applicability helper is still not wired into the release builder (CORE-06).
summary: Placeholders: added -nan, <missing>, <undefined>, n/a, #n/a; matching is case-insensitive after NFKC (full-width) folding and zero-width removal; NA stays valid. Composite IDs are rejected when a part split on / \ : | ; , is a NaN-family or MATLAB/CSV marker (nan, -nan, <na>, <missing>, <undefined>, n/a, #n/a). none/null/nat parts are kept because a path part such as 'none' can be a real condition label. The check runs on unique values only. Each affected observation gets its own invalid_identity issue naming it. A separate file-level placeholder_identity_in_file issue keeps every observation in that file ineligible, because a detached placeholder row may belong to any observation; this preserves the verifier's fail-closed test. A stringified missing task_id is invalid_metadata. profile_applicability_gaps(config) lists tasks of a reviewed/approved profile with no nonempty applicability block. G7: _nonempty_strings checks unique values as plain objects and groupby uses observed=True, so single- and multi-category identities are assessed like strings with no FutureWarning.

not_checked: No research data read. The effect of the wider placeholder and composite rules on existing converted exports is unknown until a bounded pilot re-assessment under the guarded launcher.
Composite parts joined by '_', '-', '.' or whitespace (e.g. AB01_NaN) are not split, so that nan_trial and NaT-7 stay valid. 'None'/'null' path parts are also not rejected.

Release sort order for categorical identities whose dictionary is not lexical (e.g. Parquet written by another tool) was not tested. The builder sorts the filtered export by the identity columns, which for categoricals follows category order. Only row order could differ, not content.

Optional: exclusions.parquet could carry time_lineage columns (from CORE-01).

It also says what is accepted on purpose: None/null/NaT parts, empty parts (URLs, drive letters, absolute paths, AB01//t1), and anything joined by _ - . or spaces. Each accepted case is pinned by a fixture.
